content.thinking:
I'm planning the full scene design in one pass: a mossy boulder with a red panda standing on it in a neutral four-legged pose, Genshin-style, working out proportions and stance before writing any code.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton rig — hips as root, spine chain curving into a chest joint, then a neck chain extending to the head — figuring out how many path points and joint names each chain needs so the tip aligns correctly without leaving a dangling joint.

I'm then planning the body geometry as separate swept sections: one sweep over the spine chain for the torso, and another over the neck chain for the head/neck area, using distinct radii so the seams blend naturally at the shared joints.

For the hips and tail, I'm defining a hips root joint and a separate tail chain curving up and back from the rear of the body, giving the stocky red panda frame its characteristic bushy tail base.

I'm shaping the tail to curl slightly upward in an S-curve for balance, tapering its radius toward the tip, then painting alternating rust and cream ring stripes along its length with a darker band at the very end.

Now I'm positioning the four legs, starting with the front shoulders and paws resting against the stone surface, adjusting the stone's top height so the paws sink naturally onto it.

Still working out the limb geometry...

Legs should be dark brown-black with paws getting small toe bumps and tiny cream claws for the semi-retractile red panda look. I also need to sort out parenting—hind limbs attach to the hip joint, front limbs to the chest joint on the spine chain.

Now for the head: positioning the skull sphere scaled wide for that broad red panda face with cheek tufts, adding a cream muzzle sphere pushed forward with a black nose. The ears need to be large rounded triangles made from extrusions, black on the outside with cream fur tufts inside, oriented to face forward using the correct normal direction based on the side sign.

Working out the ear outline points and mirroring logic...

Now I'm thinking about the face details: eyes placed on the skull sphere using anime-style decals, with amber-toned irises and the characteristic reddish-brown tear markings below the eyes that red pandas have against their white facial fur. I'm positioning the eyes at a slight outward angle and elevation on the skull surface.

For the head fur coloring, I'm working out a position-based paint pattern — white/cream fur on the cheeks and muzzle, with rust coloring on the forehead, using a height-based threshold along the vertical axis to blend between the two.

For the muzzle, I'll add a scaled cream/white sphere positioned forward and down from the head center, with a small black sphere at the tip for the nose, keeping the jaw as a separate piece.

Building the jaw next: a joint parented to the head, with a smaller cream sphere forming the lower jaw, a dark rod for the mouth line, and tiny cone shapes for small fangs, keeping the mouth closed overall. I'm setting up head orientation and the explicit coordinate for the head center so other parts can reference it directly.

Now I'm working out the neck chain with two intermediate points leading up to a head joint, computing the skull center and radii from the head's position, and planning cheek tufts as small cream cone spikes on either side of the face. For body coloring I'm setting up a red panda palette—rusty back, dark brown/belly countershading, and a jagged fur-edge transition between the two tones along the body.

Legs get their own gradient from rust at the hip fading to dark brown toward the paw, applied consistently across all four limbs. I'm also planning to scatter small tuft-shaped SVG cards across the body surface for texture, tinted in a rust color, with randomized placement, sizing, and leaning/bending parameters to give the fur some natural variation.

For the mossy stone, I'm sketching a lathed boulder shape with a narrower top and wider base, faceted with a handful of segments, then blending mossy green on the upper surfaces into grey stone on the sides using a noise-based paint function that mixes the normal direction with some organic variation to create a natural moss-growth pattern.

That's too tight, so I'm enlarging the stone's top radius to 0.26 and adjusting the lathe profile points accordingly to give the panda's feet enough clearance at y=0.31.

Now I'm recalculating leg proportions, shortening them to match a realistic red panda stance, raising the body's spine position slightly, and recomputing shoulder and paw joint coordinates to make sure the limb length stays within the target distance.

For decoration, I'm scattering small moss tufts, mushrooms, pebbles, and a leaf around the stone base, plus a few bamboo leaf cards for the panda to eat, aiming for that whimsical Genshin-style charm with subtle glowing accents.

Now I'm thinking of adding a glowing dendro crystal cluster (octahedron, green-cyan) at the stone base, and dressing up the panda with a cute gold-trimmed teal scarf complete with a bell and tassel, sweeping a golden collar ring around its neck.

Placing that collar loop precisely matters — I need the loop anchored partway along the neck's sweep path (around 40% in) so the cutting plane stays inside the tube rather than slicing at a cap boundary, which risks missing the mesh entirely. Going with a point-and-tangent frame from that location to keep the collar sweep stable before thickening it into the teal-and-gold band.

Skipping rods, I'll add a tassel using small gold/teal cone spikes hanging from the bell's position. Then I'm checking the neck sizing against the head proportions.

Now I'm defining a body radius function that varies smoothly with sine for a slight taper, keeping the color count under limit since paint colors don't count separately. For eyes, I'm picking an amber iris color consistent with the anime eye style, deciding whether to add blush.

For the skull, I'm setting up a surface decal pipeline: creating the skull part, getting its surface, finding a hit point near the eye location, and placing the eye decal there with mirroring. I'm keeping the brow flag off but considering small cream dot spheres above the eyes to mimic the red panda's pale brow markings, plus a simple black nose sphere and thin whisker rods sweeping from the muzzle.

Now I'm working out paw details—placing a dark scaled sphere at each limb's tip joint, then adding small toe spheres and cream claw spikes offset in front using simple literal coordinate math rather than a generic loop helper.

Checking that the paw bottoms sink slightly into the stone surface given its lathe profile, then setting up hind limb proportions with a longer plantigrade foot scale and positioning the hind feet further back. I'm also setting up the hind-leg IK chain with hip, knee, and foot joints bending forward, plus adding a rust-colored thigh mass sphere at the hip joint for bulk.

Now I'm working out the tail coloring, planning alternating rust and darker rust stripe rings with a cel-shaded, zigzag-edged pattern to mimic natural ring fur texture.

Setting tail joint radii to taper from fat to thin for that bushy red panda look, and sketching a gentle upward S-curve for the tail pose coordinates.

Now I'm chaining the skeleton from hips up through spine into chest, then neck, aligning each joint's parent and position so the body reads correctly, and placing the head joint with an offset skull center so the proportions sit naturally.

I'm then adding the jaw as a child of the head, positioning lower jaw, muzzle, and nose as separate mesh parts attached to the jaw bone, and checking that their y-coordinates don't cause the upper muzzle and lower jaw to overlap awkwardly — adjusting the jaw's vertical placement to fix the mouth gap.

Working through whether to add a mouth line or inner mouth sphere, I decide to skip both for simplicity and rely on the jaw's seam for mouth definition, then move on to placing eyes using angular coordinates around the skull.

Now I'm working out ear placement and shape—rust-colored outer ears with cream inner fluff positioned at the skull's top corners—plus cheek tuft spikes made of small white extrusions along the jawline. I'm also deciding to skip extra forehead details, add a dark chest bib and belly shading, and plan a teal-and-gold collar accent before moving on to the stone base and surrounding mushroom decorations.

For the mushrooms, I'm lathing a simple cap shape with a cream stem and red cap decorated with white spots, then thinking through the rigging: since mushrooms and stone props shouldn't move with the panda's hips, I need a separate static joint—maybe making a "base" joint the actual root instead of hips, so the panda's body is a child of that stationary ground anchor.

Now I'm working on moss tufts scattered across the stone surface, filtering points by height and placing small leaf-blade card clusters with varied lean, bend, and spin for a natural look, tinted green.

I'm adding scattered pebbles and tiny flowers on the moss patches—small sphere heads in yellow or gold with surrounding petal rings for a touch of color near the hit points.

Since the red panda eats bamboo, I'm thinking of adding a small bamboo shoot next to the stone—a few green cylinder segments with leaf cards, positioned off to the side as a standing stalk.

Adding bamboo leaf cards...

For extra ambiance, I'm thinking of small glowing crystal clusters near the stone base in teal-green, plus tiny golden firefly spheres scattered on the moss for a magical touch, keeping the triangle budget low.

I'm also considering adding small stone bumps around the base for texture, maybe with a gold inlay ring, but that risks intersecting with the lathe geometry so I'll skip it in favor of a simpler glowing rune decal on the stone's front face instead.

Designing the rune svg with teal strokes...

I need to be careful which paint helpers I actually use, avoiding unused imports — mottle, noise, paint, gradient, furEdge, cel, animeEye, INK, zigzag. I'm setting up a stone color palette using cel-shaded paints blended with mottle for a textured rock surface.

Now I'm defining the moss paint using a noise function to create patchy variation between moss and stone colors, then setting up the body color palette with rust tones, cream, and dark accents for the creature's fur.

Still writing fur texture logic...

Still defining head paint zones...

Now I'm sketching the body sweep, whiskers as thin rods, and eye decal placement with a null check on the hit test. I'm working out the joint hierarchy -- head parented to neck, legs parented to spine/hips -- and detailing the ear geometry with bevel and smoothing settings, then setting up the bamboo stalk sweep with flat caps and small cylindrical node rings along its length.

Now I'm building leaf shapes as SVG frames with a curved teardrop outline, checking the frame function signature for positioning, and working out the bell attachment point via nearest-surface lookup on the neck sweep. I'm also figuring out collar loops -- a teal ring and thinner gold rings offset along the neck's parametric length, accounting for how the tube's diameter constrains their spacing.

Still defining color palettes and dimensions...

Now I'm setting up scatter distributions for decorative cards across the body and tail surfaces, using seeded randomness with minimum distance constraints, filtering by position, and assigning warm orange tones with directional flow for the tail cards.

I'm placing a cluster of mushrooms around the base, positioning their stems and stone bases at specific radii and painting spotted caps, then adding flat pebbles, stretched glowing crystal octahedrons with tilted rotations positioned to sit just above ground level, and finally scattering a handful of glowing firefly spheres around the whole scene.
